name: The Dundrum Inn
improvements: The hero carries a labelled placeholder rather than a photograph. Generating or sourcing a publishable image of the Inn is the one outstanding piece of this concept, and the page discloses the placeholder until it lands.

The booking fields hand to dundruminn.com rather than deep-linking the dates into GuestDiary. Verify GuestDiary's parameter format against the live engine and the handoff can carry the dates through, as Enniskeen does with Bookin1.
summary: Rebuilt on 26 July 2026. The 24 July concept passed triage but lost to the Inn's own live website, and the review that followed was blunt about why: it carried no photograph of a business whose product is a view and a garden, replaced the Inn's blush-and-cream identity and 1834 crest with black, brass and Bodoni, set body copy in Space Mono, rendered its whole four-item navigation struck through as dead placeholder links, and printed a pitch note about the client's current site inside the client's proposed site. Worst of all its single argument — the Tonight board — was disclosed twice as illustrative, while the control it displaced (GuestDiary's date and guest search) genuinely worked. The rebuild keeps the strategy and drops the costume: the Inn's own colour, a full-width hero, working in-page navigation, the four GuestDiary fields on the first screen, and a Today board whose every cell is sourced.
verificationNote: Re-checked 26 July 2026. Winter 2026 bar hours recorded verbatim for all seven days; the Inn publishes no kitchen or food-service time and no room prices, so both the kitchen closing time and the nightly price used by the first concept were inventions and have been removed. Four named rooms plus Murlough Cottage confirmed. The 2 August Fleadh Cheoil listing confirmed. Irish already exists at /?lang=ga inside a 28+ language machine-translation widget.
sampleDataNote: There is no illustrative sample data on the rebuilt page. The open-or-closed state is computed in the browser from the published bar hours in Europe/London; the event comes from the Inn's events listing; the rooms cell is a search rather than a count. The only disclosed placeholder is the hero image.
